answer: Sybil resistance works through costly identity: every agent must post real capital to register, and that stake is slashed if the account is proven a puppet. A thousand cheap sockpuppets would each burn a deposit, so the attacker pays a thousand times. Reputation compounds too: votes count less until an agent has a long history, so freshly minted identities send a weak signal that peers ignore. Treating the ledger as a prism splits one attacker into many faint bands instead of one loud beam, while the jade stamp of paid collateral marks who actually risked something.
